name: Cable Straight-Arm Pulldown
summary: A cable isolation exercise that targets the latissimus dorsi by extending the shoulders through a wide arc with straight arms.

setup: Attach a straight bar or wide handle to the high pulley of a cable station.
Grasp the bar with an overhand, shoulder-width grip.
Step back a couple of feet to create tension on the cable, hinge forward slightly at the hips, and maintain a soft bend in your knees and elbows.
steps: Keeping your arms fixed with only a slight, unchanging bend at the elbows, pull the bar down in a sweeping arc toward your thighs.
Contract your lats firmly as the bar approaches your hips.
Control the bar as it travels back along the same path overhead until you feel a deep stretch in your lats.
Stop when your hands are slightly above eye level before initiating the next repetition.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you sweep the bar down toward your thighs, and inhale as you return the bar overhead under control.
cues: Drive your hands toward your pockets.
Lock your elbows in place throughout.
Keep your chest proud and brace your core.

common_faults.fault: Bending and extending the elbows, turning the movement into a triceps pushdown.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a fixed, soft elbow angle throughout the entire range of motion and move purely from the shoulders.

common_faults.fault: Using excessive body English and swinging the torso.
common_faults.correction: Lock your torso at a slight forward angle and keep your core braced to isolate the back muscles.

precautions: Do not allow the weight stack to pull your shoulders into painful hyperflexion at the top of the movement.
